description: Backend SEO enhancements: topic-level sitemap expansion with per-topic URLs, changefreq on all sitemap entries, FAQ auto-generation in content pipeline, and JSON Feed + per-subject RSS feed endpoints.
steps: In apps/backend/app/api/v1/seo.py, add a new sitemap endpoint `@router.get('/sitemap-topics.xml')` that generates a sitemap with individual URLs for each published topic. URL format: `{BASE_URL}/render/{board}/{class_level}/{subject}/{chapter}#topic-{topic_slug}` (using the fragment identifier for deep-linking). Use the KnowledgeObject model's metadata.topic field or query the Chapter model's published_topics. Each topic entry should include <lastmod>, <changefreq>weekly</changefreq>, and <priority>0.6</priority>. Use the same caching pattern as other sitemaps.
Update the SITEMAP_INDEX_XML in seo.py to include the new topics sitemap: add `<sitemap><loc>{base_url}/sitemap-topics.xml</loc></sitemap>`.
Update apps/frontend/public/_routes.json to add '/sitemap-topics.xml' to the exclude array so it bypasses the worker and gets served as a passthrough.

In apps/backend/app/api/v1/seo.py, add a JSON Feed 1.1 endpoint at `@router.get('/feed.json')`. The JSON Feed spec (https://www.jsonfeed.org/version/1.1/) requires: version, title, home_page_url, feed_url, items[]. Query published KnowledgeObjects (or Chapters), generate items with id, url, title, content_text (first 500 chars of body), date_published, date_modified, tags. Limit to 50 most recent. Return as JSON Response with content_type='application/feed+json'.

In apps/backend/app/api/v1/seo.py, add an RSS feed endpoint at `@router.get('/feed.xml')` that generates an RSS 2.0 XML feed of the most recent 50 published chapters/knowledge objects. Include: <channel> with title, link, description, language, lastBuildDate; <item> entries with title, link, description, pubDate, guid. Use the same caching pattern.

In apps/backend/app/api/v1/seo.py, add a per-subject RSS feed endpoint at `@router.get('/feed/{subject_slug}.xml')` that filters published content by subject slug. Same RSS 2.0 format as above but filtered to a single subject.

In apps/backend/app/main.py, add a second router mount for feed routes: `app.include_router(seo.router, prefix='', tags=['SEO Feeds'])` so that /feed.xml and /feed/<name>.xml are accessible at root paths (the worker proxies to these paths without rewriting). Note: existing endpoints like /sitemap*.xml will also be accessible at root which is fine since the worker already handles that rewrite.

In apps/frontend/public/_headers, add cache headers for the JSON feed: `/api/v1/seo/feed.json` with Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600, s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=3600 and Content-Type: application/feed+json.

In apps/backend/app/services/content_generation.py, in the `generate_notes` method, after generating English content and metadata, add FAQ generation: use vertex_client.generate() with a prompt asking for 5 FAQ Q&A pairs about the chapter topics. Parse the response into a list of {question, answer} dicts. Store in chapter.faq_jsonld field. This ensures newly generated chapters automatically have FAQ data for the frontend FAQPage schema.

In apps/frontend/public/_worker.js, update the SEO_PASSTHROUGH_RE regex to also match `/api/v1/seo/feed.json` path so the JSON feed gets proxied correctly. Add `|api\/v1\/seo\/feed\.json` to the regex pattern.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/v1/seo/sitemap-topics.xml returns valid XML with per-topic URLs including lastmod, changefreq, and priority
Sitemap index includes the new topics sitemap entry
GET /api/v1/seo/feed.json returns valid JSON Feed 1.1 with version='https://jsonfeed.org/version/1.1', title, items array
GET /api/v1/seo/feed.xml (also accessible at /feed.xml via worker proxy) returns valid RSS 2.0 XML
Feed endpoints use the same caching pattern as sitemaps (10min TTL)
content_generation.py generate_notes() now also generates faq_jsonld
verification: Run: cd apps/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -v 2>&1 | tail -30 (if tests exist)
Run: cd apps/backend && python -c "from app.api.v1.seo import router; print([r.path for r in router.routes])" to verify routes are registered
Run: cd apps/frontend && npx vitest run 2>&1 | tail -20
findings: All 4 new endpoints verified: /sitemap-topics.xml, /feed.xml, /feed/{subject_slug}.xml, /feed.json. Root router mount added in main.py. Worker regex updated with feed.json and contentTypeForSeo updated to return application/feed+json for JSON feed paths. FAQ generation added to content_generation.py generate_notes method. Python AST parse and Node --check both pass. No pre-existing test suite for seo.py so verification was syntax + route registration check.
